I am 69 this year. I have worked these 2 mu for 50 years. I only finished primary school. Everything I know, I learned by doing it and watching the old farmers and my neighbors. My wife and I manage the land. My son works construction in Shijiazhuang and sends some money home, but this farm is still our rice bowl. I don't change what works.

For wheat: I rotary till the land in early October, then broadcast the seed. I use improved seed, about 25 jin per mu. I buy it from the dealer in Quzhou town. For fertilizer, at sowing I put down one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer for the 2 mu, plus half a bag of diammonium phosphate. That is my base. Then at jointing time in April, I spread about 35 jin of urea per mu. I know fertilizer costs money — urea went up again — but if I put too little and the crop is thin, that is a disaster. A bad harvest means I have to buy grain. So I put enough. I irrigate three times: wintering water before the freeze, reviving water in March, and jointing water. I don't do more because the electricity for the well pump costs too much and my legs hurt walking the field. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray once more. Last year I got about 460 jin per mu. This year I hope for 480 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

For maize: Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize seed, about 5 jin per mu. I don't till the land — no time between harvest and planting, and the wheat stubble helps keep moisture. I put some compound fertilizer in the seed row when planting, about half a bag for the 2 mu. Then at big trumpet stage, I topdress with about 30 jin urea per mu. Two irrigations: one after planting if it is hot and dry, and one at big trumpet. Two sprays: one for weeds, one for corn borer. I expect about 520 jin per mu.

I watch what Lao Wang and the others do. If they buy more fertilizer, I think about it. But my land is only 2 mu. Every jin of urea is real money out of my pocket. Still, better safe than sorry on fertilizer. That is what 50 years has taught me.
